dtc.priority: OpenAI has pulled back on in-chat Instant Checkout — ChatGPT now sends buyers back to the merchant's own storefront to finish the purchase (Modern Retail / CNBC, Mar 2026). Reframe every client conversation today: the job is no longer 'get checkout inside ChatGPT,' it's 'be cited in ChatGPT AND convert when the buyer lands on your store.' Audit product-data structure and on-site conversion together — they just merged into one deliverable.

landscape.headline: OpenAI retreats on Instant Checkout — purchases now finish on the merchant's own storefront
landscape.body: OpenAI pivoted away from completing purchases inside ChatGPT. Shopify products still surface in ChatGPT conversations, but buyers now check out on the brand's own store (in-app browser or a new tab). Implication: the storefront and its product data must be both AI-citation-ready and conversion-ready, because the buyer lands back on-site. Use this in every audit.

landscape.headline: Shopify pushes 'agentic storefronts' — 1M+ merchants (Glossier, SKIMS, Vuori) to be discoverable in ChatGPT
landscape.body: Shopify told merchants their products will soon be discoverable and purchasable inside ChatGPT via new 'agentic storefronts,' built on the OpenAI/Stripe Agentic Commerce Protocol. The window for $200K–$2M founder brands is to get product data structured and citation-clean before the rush.

landscape.headline: AI-attributed Shopify orders up 11x (Jan '25 → Mar '26); AI search converts ~2x organic
landscape.body: AI referral traffic to retail grew 693% over the 2025 holiday season and AI-attributed Shopify orders rose ~11x. AI-search recommendations reportedly convert at about twice the rate of traditional organic. The revenue case for GEO is now a concrete number to put in every proposal.

landscape.headline: Perplexity Merchant Program is free; audience skews high-income — strong fit for higher-AOV brands
landscape.body: Perplexity charges merchants nothing for participation or placement. Its audience skews ~80% college-educated and ~65% high-income — the best buyer demographic of any AI engine, and potentially the highest-converting channel for research-intensive or higher-priced products. Add it to every audit's channel map.

topIdea.label: Validated Business Idea #1
topIdea.title: AI Storefront Readiness Audit
topIdea.body: A $497 productized audit scoring a Shopify store on the two jobs that now matter together: AI citation-readiness (product schema, llms.txt completeness, OAI-SearchBot/PerplexityBot access) and on-site conversion-readiness for buyers arriving from ChatGPT and Perplexity. Timely because OpenAI's Instant Checkout pullback pushes the purchase back to the merchant store. Async, fixed-scope, no discovery call.

competitors.name: Mid-market GEO/AEO agencies
competitors.changed: 2026 pricing data shows mid-market GEO retainers at $2,000–$8,000/mo (some $3K–$25K) and entry programs $1,000–$2,500 — and most still require a paid discovery phase before scoping (Digital Elevator, RevvGrowth).
competitors.howToWin: Undercut the discovery-phase friction: lead with a fixed-price 48-hour diagnostic brief ($399–$497), then convert to retainer. Trust-reversal is the structural wedge they can't easily copy.

competitors.name: Enterprise AI-visibility platforms
competitors.changed: Continue concentrating upmarket on enterprise/B2B [standing positioning — no dated move this cycle].
competitors.howToWin: The $200K–$2M founder-led DTC segment remains unserved by enterprise tools. Stay narrow and own it before they reach down-market.

competitors.name: Shopify (platform itself)
competitors.changed: Agentic storefronts + auto-generated llms.txt/agents.md commoditize *basic* AI presence for merchants (Modern Retail).
competitors.howToWin: Shift the value to completeness and quality of the auto-generated data, plus on-site conversion — neither of which the platform audits or fixes for the merchant.

cannabis.priority: Two compliance clocks just hit: New York's updated PLMA advertising/labeling rules became enforceable June 3, 2026 (NY OCM), and the DEA's expedited Schedule III rescheduling hearing begins June 29 (DOJ). Tell every regulated client to re-audit claim language now — email subject lines, product copy, and AI-readable descriptions — before rescheduling headlines drive a wave of non-compliant 'medical benefit' messaging.

landscape.headline: DEA Schedule III rescheduling hearing begins June 29, 2026 — marketing implications loom
landscape.body: DOJ/DEA placed FDA-approved and state-licensed marijuana products in Schedule III and opened an expedited hearing (June 29) on broader rescheduling. Rescheduling may loosen some constraints but will trigger a rush of 'medical benefit' claims — most still non-compliant under state and platform rules. Position compliance-first before the wave.

landscape.headline: NY PLMA advertising/labeling amendments enforceable as of June 3, 2026
landscape.body: New York's Cannabis Control Board PLMA amendments (effective Dec 3, 2025) reached their compliance deadline June 3. NY licensees must have packaging, labeling, marketing and advertising aligned now. Audit active email/SMS flows and product pages this week — this is a concrete, billable remediation trigger.

landscape.headline: Meta bans all cannabis ads (no exceptions, Mar 2026); TikTok bans all cannabis content
landscape.body: Paid social is fully closed: Meta bans all cannabis ads with no exceptions and TikTok bans all cannabis content. Owned channels (email/SMS, loyalty) and organic GEO/AEO are the only scalable growth paths left — the structural case for the owned-channel + AI-visibility play.

topIdea.label: Validated Business Idea #1
topIdea.title: Cannabis Compliance-Safe GEO Audit
topIdea.body: A $499 audit for compliance-constrained CPG brands — scores owned-channel performance, AI visibility across legal-state queries, and claim-language compliance risk by state. Especially timely with the NY PLMA deadline (June 3) and the Schedule III hearing (June 29) putting claim language under scrutiny.

competitors.name: Springbig
competitors.changed: Platform compliance modules increasingly auto-flag non-compliant copy before send [platform tooling, not strategy].
competitors.howToWin: Springbig flags copy; it doesn't set channel strategy or build AI visibility. Sell the strategic layer on top — why the channel mix is wrong and how to earn AI citations compliantly.

competitors.name: Alpine IQ
competitors.changed: Operator/platform focus; no marketing-strategy layer [standing positioning].
competitors.howToWin: Alpine IQ serves operators; you serve founders who need strategy on top of the platform. No direct overlap.

competitors.name: Generalist fractional CMOs
competitors.changed: Rescheduling buzz is drawing generalists to claim cannabis expertise on LinkedIn without compliance depth.
competitors.howToWin: Lead with 'every recommendation is platform-compliant and state-aware.' With three-level (federal/state/platform) compliance, a generalist can't credibly claim that — it's your moat.
